items.question: What is the rationale for fetal cardiac intervention?
options: Some lesions progress in utero, and there may be a window when their effects can still be reversed
All heart lesions are easier to repair before birth
It removes the need for surgery after birth
It is proven by randomised trials
items.explanation: The rationale is progression in utero with a possible limited window for reversal.

items.question: A fetal valvuloplasty was technically successful. Can the family be told the outcome will be good?
options: No: technical success does not always mean clinical success after birth
Yes: technical success guarantees a biventricular repair
Yes, if done before 28 weeks
Only if the mother had no complications
items.explanation: Technical success does not always translate into clinical success after birth.

items.question: Aortic stenosis. Which findings suggest evolving hypoplastic left heart?
options: Retrograde arch flow, severe LV dysfunction, monophasic short mitral inflow, left-to-right flow at the foramen ovale
Antegrade arch flow and normal LV function
Right-to-left flow at the foramen ovale only
A normal mitral inflow with two waves
items.explanation: These four are the signs listed in AHA 2014 Table 16.

items.question: Which fetus could be a candidate for aortic valvuloplasty?
options: Aortic stenosis (not atresia) with antegrade flow, little subvalvar obstruction, and strong evidence of evolving HLHS
Aortic atresia with no antegrade flow
Mild aortic stenosis with a normal left ventricle
Any fetus with a small left ventricle
items.explanation: Candidates need stenosis with antegrade flow, minimal subvalvar obstruction and strong evidence of evolving HLHS.

items.question: HLHS: which findings indicate clinically important atrial restriction?
options: Greater pulmonary venous flow reversal in atrial contraction, and reduced vasoreactivity to maternal hyperoxygenation
Forward pulmonary venous flow throughout the cycle
A large foramen ovale with right-to-left flow
Normal fetal heart rate
items.explanation: Greater reversal of pulmonary venous flow and reduced vasoreactivity to hyperoxygenation indicate important restriction.

items.question: Pulmonary atresia with intact septum. When may fetal intervention be lifesaving?
options: With severe tricuspid regurgitation and hydrops
In every case
Only when the right ventricle is normal size
Never
items.explanation: Intervention is controversial; only a small subset should be considered, and it may be lifesaving with severe TR and hydrops.

items.question: After fetal aortic valvuloplasty, where should the baby be delivered?
options: At a specialised congenital heart centre
At the local hospital
At home
Anywhere with a neonatologist
items.explanation: Delivery and management at a specialised congenital heart centre are recommended.
